$data.description: Reusable contracts for observed Command Hub facts supplied by the harness rather than authored into a version.

lf-worktree.description: Current worktree evidence keyed by the id of its authored lf-worktree seat.

instructions.coordinator:
After worktree evidence changes, replace the complete page-bound source snapshot rather than republishing it as prose or appending an event:

```bash
leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id> --file worktrees.json
```

Read `data_bindings` from `leaf page state "$PAGE"` to find source ids using the `lf-worktree` contract and their consuming widget ids. `worktrees.json` is an object keyed by authored worktree widget id. Each value carries `branch`, `base`, `head`, non-negative `ahead`, `behind`, `additions`, `deletions`, and `commits`, a `tests` value of `passing`, `failing`, `running`, or `not-run`, an RFC 3339 `observedAt` timestamp with a timezone, and optional `files` and `diff` strings. Keep a key stable for the same worktree, and give a different worktree a new authored lf-worktree id; a reused id would attach old comments to the wrong worktree. Gather these facts with harness tools; Leaf validates, transports, and presents them but does not run git or inspect worker directories.

$command.description: The optional Command Hub projection. Each widget names the general role it plays and the attributes that carry that role's state. A goal or worker state attribute is backed by exactly one widget-unit value record in x-state, which is also the role's report verb when it declares `writer: "agent"`, and its module presents the widgetController reading, so the projection consumes one immutable application epoch rather than rendered attributes. Later packages may add their own tag entries under widgets without teaching Leaf's kernel their names.

lf-roster.description: A view of multiple workers, their durable remits, and their current activity.
lf-roster.x-example: wren Holds the feeder rebuild end to end. finch Baffles are fitted and green; the work is yours to read. junco Free — nothing assigned since the corpus snapshot.

lf-agent.description: One worker’s identity, durable remit, current state, and reported activity.
lf-agent.x-instructions: Lead with a `<strong>` name matching the worker's reporting identity, then explain its durable remit. Within lf-command, place the worker directly under the command for project-wide work or under the narrowest task covering its remit. on is its current focus within that remit, not a role; an idle worker or broad coordinator need not invent one. Keep branch and worktree evidence in a page-bound data source. Give user work a nested Ask.

lf-tasks.description: A hierarchy of work with ownership, status, and progress derived from its tasks.
lf-tasks.x-instructions: Write the work's actual decomposition as nested lf-task elements rather than flattening it. Keep each task's id stable across revisions so comments remain attached.
lf-tasks.x-example:
Rebuild the feeders Two of four mounted. Replace the mounts Fit squirrel baffles Ready for review.

Are the baffles ready?

Approve Request changes Heat the bird bath Waiting on a transformer delivery.

lf-command.description: A goal-first command surface combining a work tree, its workers, and shared progress readings.
lf-command.x-instructions: Write one plan tree and place each worker once at the narrowest level matching its durable remit. Use on only for the worker's current focus inside that remit. Keep roster and Ask inventory as derived readings rather than authoring duplicate lists. Use lf-command-readings, named by readings, when the readings belong beside the tree instead of above it.
lf-command.x-example: lead Coordinates the whole garden. Rebuild the feeders w-1 Fitting the baffles.

lf-command-readings.description: A separate placement for a command’s progress, stopped work, and live worker readings.
lf-command-readings.x-instructions: Author it empty, with an id, and name that id in the readings of the one command it presents. Place it in the rail of a wide page when the tree belongs in the body; otherwise the command presents the same readings at its head.
lf-command-readings.x-prepaint:
Outcome

  
0 running0 workers0 quiet0 stopped
lf-command-readings.x-example: Rebuild the feeders

lf-task.description: One goal or piece of work, with ownership, status, and optional nested subgoals.
lf-task.x-instructions: Lead with a `<strong>` title, followed by prose and then its child tasks. Explain the blocker in prose when status is blocked. Status describes the work; put work for the user in a nested Ask instead. A worker's status report is provisional; a stamped version absorbs or overrules it through overruled (read $report).

lf-worktree.description: A stable, commentable address for observed worktree evidence supplied by the harness.
lf-worktree.x-instructions: Keep one empty, stable element beside each worker whose evidence the harness can inspect, binding source to the worktree snapshot. Reuse a source id when widgets read the same snapshot; give independent feeds different ids. Give a replacement worktree a new element id so old comments cannot attach to different work.
lf-worktree.x-example: wren Owns the feed rebuild.
